M O R E   M A I L ! !

  Christmas, 1993     Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Miles Kinloch........03    05
 Rick Schuitemaker....07    09
 Nigel Cattell........10    14
 Fred Ridout..........15    17
 Dick Grimmer.........18     -
 George Munro.........20    23
 Tony Wilson..........25    29
 Andy Davis...........30    34
 Bob Bates............35    36

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

About the Caps Lock puzzle in
Screen Maker, I think I know
what is happening and thought
I'd write in to say.

It's all to do with system vari-
able 23658 and the way it works,
because it's not only Caps Lock
(bit 3) it controls.Problems can
sometimes arise when other bits
are in use by the ROM, as the
value PEEKed there would then be
other than 8 or 0. Bit 4, for
instance, is used to signal the
lower screen is in use. So, when
the cursor is on the bottom two
lines,PEEK 23658 will be 16 with
Caps off and 24 with Caps on.
That seems to be the cause of
the problem.

One possible solution might be
to use the ROM call RANDOMIZE
USR 4317 to toggle Caps Lock
on/off. If you delete line 320
altogether and alter line 310
to the following, it should then
work:-

310 IF i$=CHR$ 6 THEN RANDOMIZE
USR 4317: GO TO 280

Hope this will be of some
help.

           Regards,

         Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

In practice,it is extremely rare
for POKE 23658,8 to be a problem
and is alright for use in 999
out of a thousand programs. This
is the first case of conflict I
have come across in ten years!

However,one needs to be aware of
it. The USR call is fine if you
just want to toggle CAPS on and
off but not in a program where
you need to DEFINITELY switch
CAPS ON at a certain point
because it might be ON already
in which case the USR call will
switch it off.

Another way to ONLY switch ON if
currently OFF(ie,ensure ON) is..


LET ON = INT((PEEK 23658/8)- 2 *
INT((PEEK 23658/8)/2))

IF NOT ON THEN POKE 23658, PEEK
23658 + 8

It simply test bit 3 first and
adds 8 to whatever is there ONLY
if bit 3 is zero.

It can be reversed to switch OFF
using... IF ON THEN POKE 23658,
PEEK 23658 - 8.

                          Brian

From Rick Schuitemaker, HOLLAND

Dear Chezron,

--TABLOID on a 24 pin printer.--

The difference between a 9-pin
and 24-pin printer is the number
of pins and the space between
pins(24 pins=1/60",9 pins=1/72")
so 24/216" line feed should be
20/180" for a 24-pin printer.

To work with TABLOID, the line-
feed setting needs to be
changed. We can do so in line
1605 of the CONTENTS program.

1605 GO SUB VAL "9991": POKE VAL
"64817", VAL "20": .............
....(same as before)..........


COPY ALL from OUTLET 75 did not
work. The interface must be off
so the printer is controlled
directly from the program. Line
9010 needs POKE @6,1 to disable
the +D interface. With the
interface on the program does
not work.

          Yours truly,

             Rick Schuitemaker

Brian Cavers > Rick Schuitemaker

Thanks Rick.

Sorry about the COPYALL error.It
is a victim of our not having a
24-pin printer to test it!

However, COPYALL is for use on
various Spectrum systems so POKE
@ is not appropriate on all and
the changes need to be in our
standard printer set up routine
between lines 9881 to 9890.

I am making the changes myself
and putting the new version in
this month's ADDENDERS.

                   Brian

From N.R.A. Cattell, WALSALL

REF: REPLY TO NIGEL CATTELL,
ISSUE 74 PAGE 48

Dear Saviours of the Spectrum,

The mists have cleared, my
reservation at the Home for the
Bothered & Bewildered has been
cancelled. Your reply to my last
missive triggered something in
my deep subconcious - "Carriage
Return" was the trigger.

Before using my printer there is
a set up mode to go through,dur-
ing which 18 separate defaults
are offered to the user. I last
went through them some two years
ago and have left them alone
ever since.

I had wrongly assumed that if a
program like PCG's DTP worked OK
then the defaults that I had set
were good for all the other
printing that I would do (deep
breath now). I was wrong.

I went back to set up mode and
checked the defaults concerning
line feeds and carriage returns.
I found that in answer to the
default LF=LF I had accepted
that and and for carriage return
I had accepted CR=CR , This must
be where the problem lay. I
decided to alter them both to
LF=LF+CR and CR=CR+LF.

I then loaded "TOPCAL" and got a
lovely print out with everything
as it should be.


I then decided to print out the
mail using "TABLOID" (may bless-
ings fall upon him that wrote
it)and low and behold my printer
carried on printing after the
end the page.

I checked Paper End Detection
had been set to "YES". It was
so I altered CR=CR+LF TO CR=CR
and yes - it worked - no more
printout problems and deep joy
all around.

Just one point I'd like to make
about my last letter since it
may have caused some confusion,
you referred to IBM mode, but I
had written BIM mode (BIT IMAGE
MODE) which is graphics mode. I
have never used IBM mode and I
don't see any reason to do so.

I have enclosed my original text
file so that you can see that
I'm not telling Porkys.

Thanks for the help and I'm now
looking through all my back
issues of "OUTLET" for things
that print out (thank goodness
Brian Gaff has a re-inking
service) [see OUTBOARD - Ed].

Now, if only there was a way to
print out those lovely opening
screen$ without a Multiface????

Yes, alright, I'm going now
before I am declared Persona Non
Grata at Outlet HQ.Thanks again.

                   NIGEL

Brian Cavers to Nigel Cattell

Glad to hear that all is now
O.K. Sorry about the mixup with
the "BIM"/"IBM". That was my
fault. "BIM" is not a term I am
familiar with and I just assumed
you were mis-spelling "IBM"!

One way to print the title page
is to RESET and MERGE the loader
("AUTOLOAD" on +D, "DISK" on+3,
"OUTLET 76" on tape) and enter:
GOSUB 1000:COPY EXP(+3) or...
GOSUB 1000:SAVE SCREEN 2 (+D).

Don't enter GO SUB 1000 and then
enter COPY separately else the
bottom two lines will be lost.It
must be entered in one go with a
colon in between.
                        - Brian

           F. Ridout
         60 Queensfield
       Swindon, WILTSHIRE
            SN2 6SY

Dear Brian,

Thanks for your extensive reply.
[OUTLETTERS 74].

To start at the top, the Genius
Mouse values are left/right
0-255 and up/down 0-255. Also it
seems that Datel's addresses are
the wrong way around [left/right
coordinates should be IN 64479
and up/down IN 65503 - Ed] I
think that as the program works
and the mouse performs OK on ART
STUDIO it is Datel's error. The
buttons are correct.


I assume the triangle flashing
is due to the speed of BASIC and
error produced on going outside
the screen border needs some
protection. Anyway thank you for
putting me on the right track.

Now, if I am permitted one last
question, is it possible to wire
a TIMEX SINCLAIR 2040 printer to
run off the RS232 port in 128
mode as I only use the printer
for LLISTing and memo notes and
not for more serious uses? You
can use my full address as maybe
someone out there knows the
answer. Thank you for all your
help

                   FRED
                (F Ridout)


Brian Cavers to Fred Ridout

Glad to hear my routine to use
the Genius Mouse from BASIC
worked and I hope you can make
some use of it.

As for connecting a TIMEX 2040
printer to a +2 RS232 port, I
can say unequivob... uniquivab..
unequivercobbly (well actually I
can't say it at all). I can say
quite clearly that it is certain
beyond all doubt that you can't
(probably).
                         Brian

From Dick Grimmer, MERSEYSIDE

Dear Ron and Brian,

I must indicate how very much I
enjoyed reading OUTLET No.74
which covered quite a lot of
ground of much interest. I liked
your resume of the PC, partly
instigated by Malcolm Goodman's
letter to you in that issue.

The details you kindly outlined
have actually put me off
venturing into the PC scene - in
particular, the relatively high
cost of possessing the necessary
items of equipment and apparent
not so"user-friendliness" for my
taste; at least more complicated
than the good old Spectrum.


I would also like to mention
both Malcolm Perry and Brian
Gaff as two of your many contri-
butors both of whom I have had
some correspondence with from
time to time. Let me say how
very kind and friendly chaps
they both are and always quite
willing to go out of their way
to be helpful to people to
overcome problems of one kind or
another -pretty much in the same
category as yourselves and that
is saying something!

My very best wishes to you all.

        Your sincerely,

         Dick Grimmer

From George Munro, LONDON NW3.

Dear Ron,

I have now acquired a Sam Coupe
and it is in connection with
this, that I write asking for
your help, or help from any of
your readers or contributors.

My problem is this, the Sam runs
perfectly happily when I use a
television set, sound is perfect
etc., but when I try to use the
Sam with my Microvitec Cub I
cannot get any sound out of it,
although I used the same succ-
essful set up as with my 128K
and 48K Spectrums ie, connecting
the Cassette plug to a CPD8300
WH.Smith Data Recorder which has
a sound amplifier.

May I hasten to add that the
cassette connection quite
happily loads programs to the
Sam so there is no fault at that
source.

I did try connecting the tele-
vision lead from the Sam power
output to the data recorder but
this only produced a low
sounding hum.

Perhaps one of your readers has
already solved this problem and
could advise me what to do; if
not, then it looks as if I shall
need to buy another monitor for
the Sam; if this turns out to be
the case I would be pleased to
hear from anyone with such an
item for sale.


My renewed congratulations on
the continuance and excellence
of OUTLET. Hopefully once I have
the Sam up and running satis-
factorily with the monitor I
could have a go at writing a
program for it.

        Yours sincerely,

        George B. Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

You appreciate we no longer do a
SAM OUTLET and do not normally
deal with SAM problems etc in
this Spectrum version. However..

The SAM tape save is different
to the Spectrum and cannot be
used as a sound output in the
same way.

Look at page 173 of your SAM
manual and you will see a
diagram of the various inputs
and outputs.

I suggest you try to connect
to pin 6 mono sound output of
the main power input socket
(the other connection to the
casing).

It will probably be easier to do
this at the other end of the
power cable (the low voltage of
course not the mains!) - ie in
the tv modulator/power supply
unit.

The other sound output is the
stereo one from the light pen
socket.

                         Brian

From A.B. Wilson, SKIPTON

Dear Chezron,

I haven't had time to keep up
with Outlet recently because
I've inherited an old Amstrad
1640 PC from work! In spite of
what people say about the
"unfriendliness" of the PC I've
found that it is possible to
organise it to make it easy to
use, but it does take a lot of
time and mental energy to do it.

I've been messing about with
GWbasic on it, and found that
fairly easy to handle, but
nowhere near as good as Uncle
Clive's Basic. String handling
can be quite tricky, especially
in an array!

If you do get around to produc-
ing a PC version of Outlet I'll
probably have to get 2 versions
each month because there is so
much good stuff on them.

How are you getting on with Mas-
terfile? I've been using it for
some years and find it extremely
easy to use. I use it for my
Scout Troop records, my massive
Book list (1500+ records), a
diary, and, of course, Outlet
details.

To economize on disc storage
space I don't keep Outlet on the
original discs. Instead, I print
out Letters, Editorial, Outclass
and that sort of thing using
your Tabloid option(beautiful!).


Then, using my Multiface 3, I
print out the Graphics screen
and Contents list as a front
page and title screens and
instructions for any programmes
I intend keeping. These are all
bound together as a magazine.


I modify some of your Basic
lines 8910 etc and 8955 and any
others as necessary to make a
stand- alone programme or to
include in one of my own menu
programmes.

Games, Music, Graphics screens,
crosswords, index, and 'serious
stuff' are all kept on separate
discs.


I don't have a Disciple, +D, or
anything like that, so I simply
discard anything to do with
them. The original Outlet discs
are then erased and kept for
other jobs. Everything is then
logged using Masterfile, making
it very easy for me to find any-
thing.

        Yours sincerely,

          Tony Wilson

Brian Cavers to Tony Wilson

Yes, I agree, BASIC on the PC is
quite naive in many respects in
comparison to Sinclair BASIC. It
seems Microsoft lack the ability
or the motivation to improve the
language or to learn from other
variants. Others blindly follow
the Microsoft standard when
creating other BASICs.

Nevertheless, QUICK BASIC has
plenty of power and one can do a
lot with it - albeit often with
more effort than the equivalent
on the Spectrum.

As for MASTERFILE, you will now
have seen we finally got it in
last month's issue!     - Brian


           Andy Davis
       Alchemist Research
       62 Tithe Barn Lane
           Woodhouse
           Sheffield
            S13 7LN


Telephone: 0764 697644 after 6pm


Dear Ron and Brian,


George Jones of Chester told me
that a reader was looking for
external +2 tape instructions.
These can be found in AlchNews
8 [OUTLET 74]



I'd also like to make advantage
of your large readership to make
an apology to Darren Randle (ex-
Rasputin PD / Sinclair News)...

Mr Carswell made an untrue
allegation in his "NEWSDESK"
tapezine stating that Mr. Randle
had "stolen" the AlchNews shell
from me.Let me clearly point out
that Mr. Randle did NOT steal
the shell, nor did he use it for
Sinclair News.

Issue 1 of Sinclair News used my
PD Tasword viewer program, but
Issues 2 and 3 used a specially
written Enigma style driver by
Dominic Morris.Besides all this,
I did not "inform" Mr Carswell
of the above statments either.


As Rasputin PD has now closed,it
shouldn't hurt Mr Randle's repu-
tation, but all the same, it is
still not nice, especially when
we have a hard enough job trying
to keep the Spectrum going.

As I have now purchased the
rights to Rasputin PD and Sinc-
lair News, OUTLET readers can
have any issues of this tape/
diskzine free of charge by send-
ing a tape / +D disk and SAE.
I've given brief details in
AlchNews 10 but space and
details were limited so I can
fill customers in more if they
write. I hope to put all the PD
from Rasputin and RAS PD, which
has also closed down, in the new
PD list by the new year.


Thankyou for your time and space
and thank you to all the good
support from the OUTLET readers!

          Best Wishes,

           Andy Davis

Brian Cavers to Andy Davis



Thanks Andy.I've passed ALCHNEWS
10 to our editor Chris Oliver
and it should be in OUTLET soon.

                   Brian

From Bob Bates, NOTTINGHAM

Dear Ron, Brian and all,

There is some very good software
beocming available in the pubic
domain, first Tasword, now
Masterfile, next Art Studio or
Artist II? There will soon be
enough to suport new [illegible]
of the Spectrum without reliance
on the original suppliers! Have
any approaches been made to the
publishers of Omnicalc, Art
Studio and Artist II? Although I
already have these programs, the
improvements that you have made
to MASTERFILE are a welcome
addition to the facilities of
the program.
                      Bob Bates.

Brian Cavers to Bob Bates

I didn't know Tasword was in the
public domain. Is that Tasword 2
or all the Taswords? What about
TASCALC, etc? Where did you hear
this as we need to be careful if
we publish anything!

I've not heard about any other
approaches to software house to
persuade them to put their soft-
ware in the public domain other
than MASTERFILE.

                          Brian.

M O R E   M A I L ! !

Christmas, 1993     Page Reply

How to write to us...02     - Miles Kinloch........03    05 Rick Schuitemaker....07    09 Nigel Cattell........10    14 Fred Ridout..........15    17 Dick Grimmer.........18     - George Munro.........20    23 Tony Wilson..........25    29 Andy Davis...........30    34 Bob Bates............35    36

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

About the Caps Lock puzzle in Screen Maker, I think I know what is happening and thought I'd write in to say.

It's all to do with system vari- able 23658 and the way it works, because it's not only Caps Lock (bit 3) it controls.Problems can sometimes arise when other bits are in use by the ROM, as the value PEEKed there would then be other than 8 or 0. Bit 4, for instance, is used to signal the lower screen is in use. So, when the cursor is on the bottom two lines,PEEK 23658 will be 16 with Caps off and 24 with Caps on. That seems to be the cause of the problem.

One possible solution might be to use the ROM call RANDOMIZE USR 4317 to toggle Caps Lock on/off. If you delete line 320 altogether and alter line 310 to the following, it should then work:-

310 IF i$=CHR$ 6 THEN RANDOMIZE USR 4317: GO TO 280

Hope this will be of some help.

Regards,

Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

In practice,it is extremely rare for POKE 23658,8 to be a problem and is alright for use in 999 out of a thousand programs. This is the first case of conflict I have come across in ten years!

However,one needs to be aware of it. The USR call is fine if you just want to toggle CAPS on and off but not in a program where you need to DEFINITELY switch CAPS ON at a certain point because it might be ON already in which case the USR call will switch it off.

Another way to ONLY switch ON if currently OFF(ie,ensure ON) is..

LET ON = INT((PEEK 23658/8)- 2 * INT((PEEK 23658/8)/2))

IF NOT ON THEN POKE 23658, PEEK 23658 + 8

It simply test bit 3 first and adds 8 to whatever is there ONLY if bit 3 is zero.

It can be reversed to switch OFF using... IF ON THEN POKE 23658, PEEK 23658 - 8.

```text
                          Brian
```

To work with TABLOID, the line- feed setting needs to be changed. We can do so in line 1605 of the CONTENTS program.

1605 GO SUB VAL "9991": POKE VAL

```text
"64817", VAL "20": .............
```

....(same as before)..........

COPY ALL from OUTLET 75 did not work. The interface must be off so the printer is controlled directly from the program. Line 9010 needs POKE @6,1 to disable the +D interface. With the interface on the program does not work.

Yours truly,

Rick Schuitemaker

Brian Cavers > Rick Schuitemaker

Thanks Rick.

Sorry about the COPYALL error.It is a victim of our not having a 24-pin printer to test it!

I am making the changes myself and putting the new version in this month's ADDENDERS.

Brian

### От Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

По поводу загадки с Caps Lock в Screen Maker: кажется, я понял, в чём дело, и решил написать об этом.

Всё дело в системной переменной 23658 и том, как она работает, ведь она управляет не только Caps Lock (бит 3). Проблемы иногда могут возникать, когда другие биты используются ROM, поскольку значение, считываемое через PEEK, тогда будет отличаться от 8 или 0. Бит 4, например, используется для индикации того, что задействована нижняя часть экрана. Поэтому, когда курсор находится на двух нижних строках, `PEEK 23658` вернёт 16 при выключенном Caps и 24 при включенном Caps. Похоже, именно это и является причиной проблемы.

Одним из возможных решений может быть использование вызова ROM `RANDOMIZE USR 4317` для переключения Caps Lock вкл/выкл. Если полностью удалить строку 320 и изменить строку 310 следующим образом, всё должно заработать:

```basic
310 IF i$=CHR$ 6 THEN RANDOMIZE USR 4317: GO TO 280
```

Надеюсь, это хоть чем-то поможет.

С уважением,  
Miles Kinloch

### Brian Cavers — Miles Kinloch

На практике ситуация, когда `POKE 23658,8` вызывает проблемы, случается крайне редко, и эта команда отлично работает в 999 случаях из тысячи программ. Это первый случай подобного конфликта, с которым я столкнулся за десять лет!

Тем не менее, об этом нужно помнить. Вызов USR хорош, если вам нужно просто переключить CAPS туда-обратно, но не подходит для программы, где требуется ОПРЕДЕЛЁННО включить CAPS в конкретный момент, поскольку он может быть уже включен — и тогда вызов USR его выключит.

Ещё один способ включить его ТОЛЬКО тогда, когда он выключен (т.е. гарантированно включить):

```basic
LET ON = INT((PEEK 23658/8)- 2 * INT((PEEK 23658/8)/2))

IF NOT ON THEN POKE 23658, PEEK 23658 + 8
```

Здесь просто сначала проверяется бит 3, и 8 прибавляется к текущему значению ТОЛЬКО в том случае, если бит 3 равен нулю.

Для выключения можно сделать наоборот: `IF ON THEN POKE 23658, PEEK 23658 - 8`.

Brian

-- TABLOID на 24-игольчатом принтере. --

Разница между 9-игольчатым и 24-игольчатым принтером заключается в количестве игл и расстоянии между ними (24 иглы = 1/60", 9 игл = 1/72"), поэтому перевод строки 24/216" для 24-игольчатого принтера должен составлять 20/180".

Чтобы программа работала с TABLOID, настройку перевода строки необходимо изменить. Это можно сделать в строке 1605 программы CONTENTS.

```basic
1605 GO SUB VAL "9991": POKE VAL "64817", VAL "20": .................(как и раньше)..........
```

COPY ALL из OUTLET 75 не сработал. Интерфейс должен быть отключен, чтобы принтер управлялся напрямую из программы. В строке 9010 требуется команда `POKE @6,1` для отключения интерфейса +D. При включенном интерфейсе программа не работает.

Искренне ваш,  
Rick Schuitemaker
